# Codex verification brief — relation map on the try-it page (commit bfcb83d)

You are an independent reviewer. Do NOT edit any tracked file. Write scratch files only under
`audit_evidence_claims/m1/`. Put your report in `audit_evidence_claims/m1/REPORT.md`.
End with exactly one line: `VERDICT: APPROVE` or `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED`.

## What was added

`src/app.py` `Engine.explore(text, per_group=30)` and `POST /api/explore`; `web/try.html` section "0. 관계 지도"
(`drawMap`, `explore`, `itemDetail`, the GKO/TKO/ACT/PH tables, click-through and the "따라온 길" trail);
`tests/test_app.py::test_explore_draws_a_drug_and_refuses_a_biosimilar`. Run tests with
`python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` (317). Start the page with `python src/app.py [port]` (use a port
other than 8765, which may already be in use) and exercise it over HTTP.

The page is for a domain reviewer to look at one node (drug, target, company, investigator, trial, disease) and
everything a live edge ties it to, grouped by relation, and to click through. It is read-only.

## The guarantees claimed (page text in section 0 and the `explore` docstring)

1. Every neighbour shown is joined to the centre by a live (not retired) edge to a live node, and the group label
   states the relation and its direction correctly (e.g. "이 약의 임상을 주관한 곳 (주관 ≠ 개발)" for
   Company -SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF-> Drug seen from the drug).
2. Details shown for a neighbour are the stored values: trial phases/status/start/title/url, sponsor trial count
   (`evidence_trials`) and sponsor class, drug trial count in the graph (EVALUATES), max phase, action type.
3. A name the question linker refuses (biosimilar, distinct product, tracer) is reported as refused, never drawn
   as the originator molecule; an unknown name says "not found".
4. Groups are ordered by size and each list keeps the `per_group` neighbours with most evidence; the page says
   when a list is cut and shows the true total.
5. Nothing is written; no model is called.

## What to verify (reproduce; cite file:line and exact inputs)

A. **Wrong relations or directions.** Any centre where an edge is grouped under the wrong label or direction,
   self-loops (src == dst), edges with both ends equal to the centre, PARENT_OF/SPONSORS/STUDIES/ASSOCIATED_WITH
   direction wording, Investigator vs Company handling, nodes whose type the tables do not cover.
B. **Name resolution.** `explore` takes the first non-refused hit of `link_entities`. Inputs with several entities
   ("osimertinib EGFR"), a refused token next to a real one ("Mvasi bevacizumab"), salts vs parents, company aliases
   with `also_matching_ids` (only the first id is drawn — is that misleading?), node ids vs names that collide,
   case/whitespace/Unicode, long inputs. Is anything drawn that the input does not name, or a refused product drawn
   as the originator?
C. **Wrong values.** Trial counts, sponsor counts, max phase and action shown versus the database
   (`data/processed/oncokg.sqlite`); retired edges/nodes leaking in; counts computed over retired edges;
   the `trials` count chunking; JSON props that are null or malformed.
D. **Cutting and ordering.** Is the "most evidence" ordering what the page says (trials are ordered by start date
   string — is that what the text implies)? Does the map's subset (`drawMap` allocation) ever hide a whole group
   or misstate totals? The Disease node (thousands of neighbours) — performance and output size.
E. **Page safety and correctness.** HTML/SVG injection from labels, titles, ids, URLs (`href` with `javascript:`?),
   edge ids in `data-id` attributes, the trail/back buttons after errors, double clicks, refused/not-found states,
   dark mode legibility is not in scope.
F. **Server.** Error handling for empty/oversized input, concurrency with the lock, behaviour when the DB has
   retired rows.
G. **Docs and wording.** Section 0 text, README/README.ko lines for `app.py`, the module docstring: do they claim
   more than the code does? Korean labels in GKO/ACT/PH that misstate the stored code.

## Approval bar

No known way for the map to show a relation that is not a live edge, a wrong direction or relation wording, a
value that differs from the stored one, a refused product drawn as the originator, or script injection. Report
should-fix items (misleading wording, cut lists without notice) separately from blockers.

---
name: review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes ??Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** ??does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** ??does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you ??run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point ??a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here ??not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) ??fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3.
- The brief: "Report ??per file/hunk where relevant ??every place the diff violates a documented standard. Cite the standard (file + the rule). Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings ??the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes ??that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing ??**Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions ??**Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

## Round 4 (audit_evidence_claims/m4) ??CHANGES REQUIRED

Shortest-span binding kept failing (wrong drug on ties, a six-token reach, qualifiers already consumed by the token pass).
Replaced by a fail-closed rule: text is cut into list items at , ; 竊?竊???and listing words; an item in which any run of
words names a distinct product or tracer has every drug in it refused (which drug the qualifier describes is not guessed);
drugs in other items, and targets/companies in the same item, still link. M4-B1 (both drugs now refused, never
BEVACIZUMAB), M4-B2 (no distance cap), M4-B3 (one pass, no pre-consumed qualifier) and the EGFR/AstraZeneca over-refusal
are covered by tests. Tests 326.

| M5-B2 | "liposomal and nanoparticle formulation of doxorubicin": "and" detached the bare qualifier | a qualifier item with no drug carries across a listing word to the next item's drugs; a product named by itself (in the index, or a known biosimilar/reformulation brand such as Mvasi, Abraxane) does not carry |

## M20-B1: 161Tb / terbium-161 labelled product selects unlabelled trastuzumab

Exact strongest input: **`trastuzumab labelled with terbium-161`**. Current direct map returns **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585 / 13 trials**, with no refusal. `Which trials evaluate trastuzumab labelled with terbium-161?` and `Who sponsors trials of trastuzumab labelled with terbium-161?` each return **12 originator evidence rows**. The paired `trastuzumab labelled with lutetium-177` refuses, with no map centre and no QA evidence.

This is a real research product, not an invented isotope/drug pairing. The primary study of Cold et al. reports DOTA-functionalized trastuzumab radiolabelled with 161Tb and compares it with native trastuzumab. It was published **2026-04-01**, before this review date. [PubMed primary abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41679917/). The equivalence of the explicit plain-English input to that labelled product is the reviewer's inference; no clinical recommendation or graph evidence is taken from the paper.

| Stage | `trastuzumab labelled with terbium-161` | `trastuzumab labelled with lutetium-177` |
|---|---|---|
| Intervention resolver | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED |
| `_resolver_blocked` | `{}` | `{}` |
| `_qualified` | false | false |
| `_item_has_isotope` | false | true |
| Actual `_marked` call | `None`, all four tokens in segment 0 | refusal |
| `_whole_name` | `None` | `None` |
| Public linker | positive Drug, no Refused | Refused only |
| Direct map | CHEMBL1201585, 13 trials | refused, no centre |
| Trial / sponsor QA | 12 / 12 evidence rows | 0 / 0 |

**Cause:** the common isotope vocabulary omits `tb` in `src/textrules.py:290-293`, and `src/query.py:124-128` omits its masses. The full-name table `src/query.py:156-162` omits `terbium`. Consequently neither the symbol rules nor the new full-name loop (`src/query.py:182-188`) can recognize it. `labelled` alone is not one of the radioactive words (`src/query.py:164-180`). The item-wide guard in `_marked` therefore returns no refusal (`src/query.py:424-426`), leaving a positive Drug for `Engine.explore` (`src/app.py:88-95`). This is broader than a punctuation spelling: these tested elements absent from all three tables receive no isotope-based refusal; an explicit recognised labelling word can still refuse them.

Corroborations in [full stage evidence](attacks/new_results.json), [compact results](attacks/new_summary.json): `161Tb trastuzumab`, `Tb-161 trastuzumab`, `[161Tb] trastuzumab`, `terbium-161 trastuzumab`, `161-terbium trastuzumab`, `trastuzumab labelled with 161-terbium`, `161Tb-labelled trastuzumab`, `trastuzumab labelled with Tb-161`, `trastuzumab labelled with 161Tb`, and `161Tb Herceptin` all draw the same originator and return 12 / 12 QA rows. `[161Tb] trastuzumab` is especially notable: intervention resolution reports **EXACT**, after losing the unrecognised bracketed isotope. `161Tb radiolabelled trastuzumab` correctly refuses via the explicit label word. The completely fused `161Tb-trastuzumab` and `[161Tb]Tb-trastuzumab` are **not_found** and are not claimed as leaks.

The same omission reproduces for `227Th trastuzumab`, `trastuzumab labelled with thorium-227`, `213Bi trastuzumab`, and `trastuzumab labelled with bismuth-213`: all 13 map trials / 12 trial evidence / 12 sponsor evidence, no refusal. These elements are also absent. The 227Th product was independently compared with cold trastuzumab in [Abbas et al., 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22214432/); a [primary 213Bi-Herceptin experiment](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15670895/) establishes the other labelled construct. [Supplement stage evidence](attacks/supplement_results.json). These are one table-coverage blocker, not separately counted defects. Scandium/holmium probes are recorded as software observations but are not needed to establish the finding.

All these inputs also leak with `HEAD^:src/query.py` substituted against current remaining modules/data. This is a counterfactual module comparison, not a complete historical deployment. Root independently owns real CLI HTTP corroboration.

    if isinstance(lifecycle,dict) and isinstance(lifecycle.get('port'),int):
        owned_ports.add(lifecycle['port'])
for port in sorted(owned_ports):
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.settimeout(.2);ports[str(port)]=sock.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1',port))!=0

links=re.findall(r'\]\(([^)]+)\)',report)
local=[s for s in links if not re.match(r'https?://',s)]
broken=[s for s in local if s!='integrity_final.json' and not (OUT/s.split('#',1)[0]).exists()]
db=hashlib.sha256((ROOT/'data/processed/oncokg.sqlite').read_bytes()).hexdigest()
status=git('status','--short')
result=dict(time=datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(),head_before=before['head'],

    changed_tracked_files=changed,missing_tracked_files=missing,new_tracked_paths=sorted(tracked-set(before['tracked_sha256'])),
    tracked_diff=git('diff','--exit-code'),staged_diff=git('diff','--cached','--exit-code'),

def post(endpoint, text):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/api/" + endpoint,
        data=json.dumps({"text": text}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        return {"endpoint": endpoint, "input": text, "status": response.status,
                "seconds": time.perf_counter() - start,
                "response": json.loads(response.read())}

with socket.socket() as sock:
    assert sock.connect_ex(("127.0.0.1", PORT)) != 0, "owned port already occupied"

with (OUT / "independent_m20_server.txt").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log:
    proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-B", "-u", "src/app.py", str(PORT)],
        cwd=ROOT, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0))
    results = []
    try:
        for _ in range(100):
            assert proc.poll() is None, "server exited"

                break
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(.1)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("server unavailable")

import json,os,subprocess,sys,time,types
OUT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent;ROOT=OUT.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT/'src'))
import query
rows=[]
for n in [125,1000]:
    kg=query.OncoKG();kg.conn.execute('PRAGMA query_only=ON')
    original=query._medical_isotope_in
    calls={'one_letter_false':0,'one_letter_true':0,'characters':0}
    def counted(key,one_letter=True):
        calls['one_letter_true' if one_letter else 'one_letter_false']+=1
        calls['characters']+=len(key)
        return original(key,one_letter)
    query._medical_isotope_in=counted
    try:
        value=' '.join(['isa']*n)
        start=time.perf_counter();entities=kg.link_entities(value);elapsed=time.perf_counter()-start
        rows.append(dict(matches=n,characters=len(value),helper_calls=calls,seconds_with_instrumentation=elapsed,entities=entities))
    finally:
        query._medical_isotope_in=original;kg.conn.close()
(OUT/'repeated_match_instrumentation.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
source=OUT/'unique_cost_http.py'

FILE src/app.py
1: """A local page for trying the pipeline by hand.
2: 
3:     python src/app.py            then open http://localhost:8765
4: 
5: A relation map (a node and the nodes live edges tie it to, a capped list per relation,
6: click to move on),
7: then four boxes: type an intervention string the way a registry would write it and see
8: how the resolver reads it, or ask a question and see the grounded answer with its
9: evidence, give a structured answer (claims citing evidence edges) and see which
10: claims the graph supports and the answer written from them, or paste free prose and
11: see what the auxiliary word-order check flags. All of them call
12: the functions the pipeline uses (resolve_drug_string, OncoKG.answer,
13: OncoKG.check_groundedness) on the built artefacts, so what the page shows is what the
14: pipeline would do. Nothing is written; the language model is never called.
15: """
16: from __future__ import annotations
17: 
18: import json
19: import sqlite3
20: import sys
21: import threading
22: from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
23: from pathlib import Path
24: 
25: sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
26: import config as C
27: import normalize as N
28: import textrules as T
29: from query import OncoKG
30: 
31: PAGE = C.WEB / "try.html"
32: PORT = 8765
33: 
34: 
35: class Engine:
36:     def __init__(self):
37:         self.kg = OncoKG()
38:         # A browser opens spare connections it may never use, which would stall a
39:         # single-threaded server; requests are threaded, the engine is not.
40:         self.kg.conn.close()
41:         self.kg.conn = sqlite3.connect(C.PROCESSED / "oncokg.sqlite", check_same_thread=False)
42:         self.kg.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
43:         self.lock = threading.Lock()
44:         self.dic = self.kg.dic
45:         self.index_keys = self.kg.index_keys
46:         target_rows, _, _ = N._load("targets")
47:         self.target_keys = N.target_guard_keys(target_rows, self.dic)
48: 
49:     def resolve(self, text: str) -> dict:
50:         out = N.resolve_drug_string(text, self.dic, self.index_keys, self.target_keys)
51:         for c in out["components"]:
52:             d = self.dic["drugs"].get(c.get("drug_id") or "")
53:             if d:
54:                 c["drug"] = {k: d.get(k) for k in
55:                              ("name", "drug_type", "max_phase_overall", "max_phase_in_nsclc")}
56:                 c["drug"]["mechanisms"] = [m.get("mechanismOfAction") if isinstance(m, dict) else m
57:                                            for m in (d.get("mechanisms") or [])][:3]
58:                 c["drug"]["trials"] = self.kg.conn.execute(
59:                     "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
60:                     (d["drug_id"],)).fetchone()[0]
61:                 par = self.dic["drugs"].get(d.get("parent_molecule") or "")
62:                 if par:
63:                     c["drug"]["parent"] = {"name": par["name"], "trials": self.kg.conn.execute(
64:                         "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
65:                         (par["drug_id"],)).fetchone()[0]}
66:             if c.get("candidates"):
67:                 c["candidate_names"] = [
68:                     (self.dic["drugs"].get(x) or {}).get("name", x) for x in c["candidates"]]
69:         return out
70: 
71:     def explore(self, text: str, per_group: int = 30) -> dict:
72:         """One live node and the live nodes its live edges tie it to, grouped by relation.
73: 
74:         `text` is a node id or a name the question linker reads as one entity. A name
75:         the linker refuses (a biosimilar, a reformulation, a tracer) is reported, never
76:         mapped to the originator. Each group keeps `per_group` neighbours, sorted as the
77:         page states: trials by start date (latest first), drugs by trials in the graph,
78:         sponsors by trials they lead, disease targets by association score. Sponsorship
79:         keeps its role (lead sponsor or collaborator)."""
80:         conn = self.kg.conn
81:         also: list = []
82:         matched = None
83:         row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
84:                            (text,)).fetchone()
85:         if row:
86:             nid = row["id"]
87:         else:
88:             ents = self.kg.link_entities(text)
89:             refused = [e for e in ents if e["type"] == "Refused"]
90:             hits = [e for e in ents if e.get("id") and e["type"] != "Refused"]
91:             if not hits:
92:                 if refused:
93:                     return {"refused": refused[0]["label"], "why": refused[0]["why"]}
94:                 return {"not_found": text}
95:             nid, matched = hits[0]["id"], hits[0].get("matched_alias") or hits[0].get("matched_text")
96:             also = [{"id": e["id"], "type": e["type"], "label": e["label"]} for e in hits[1:]]
97:             for oid in hits[0].get("also_matching_ids") or []:   # one alias, several ids
98:                 lab = conn.execute("SELECT type, label FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
99:                                    (oid,)).fetchone()
100:                 if lab and oid != nid:
101:                     also.append({"id": oid, "type": lab["type"], "label": lab["label"]})
102:             # the same words may also name an organisation or a target the linker
103:             # passed over because a drug alias came first ("Roche" is a folic acid alias)
104:             key = T.canonical_key(text)
105:             for cid in self.kg.companies.get(key, []):
106:                 if cid != nid and all(x.get("id") != cid for x in also):
107:                     lab = conn.execute("SELECT label FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
108:                                        (cid,)).fetchone()
109:                     if lab:
110:                         also.append({"id": cid, "type": "Company", "label": lab["label"]})
170:         out.sort(key=lambda g: -g["total"])
171:         props = _obj(node["props"])
172:         return {"center": {"id": node["id"], "type": node["type"], "label": node["label"],
173:                            "matched_text": matched,
174:                            "trials": trials.get(node["id"], 0) if node["type"] == "Drug" else None,
175:                            "props": {k: props.get(k) for k in
176:                                      ("max_phase_overall", "drug_type", "phases", "status",
177:                                       "title", "url", "start_date") if props.get(k) is not None}},
178:                 "also": also, "groups": out}
179: 
180:     def ask(self, question: str) -> dict:
181:         return self.kg.answer(question, use_llm=False).to_dict()
182: 
183:     def structured(self, question: str, payload: str) -> dict:
184:         """Check a structured answer (claims citing edges) and write the answer from it."""
185:         kg = self.kg
186:         entities = kg.link_entities(question)
187:         evidence = kg.retrieve(kg.classify(question, entities), entities)
188:         res = kg.verify_structured(payload, evidence)
189:         res["evidence"] = [{"edge_id": e.edge_id, "statement": e.statement} for e in evidence]
190:         return res
230:             if self.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
231:                 self._send(200, PAGE.read_bytes(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")
232:             else:
233:                 self._send(404, b"not found", "text/plain")

235:         def do_POST(self):
236:             try:
237:                 n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
238:                 body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(min(n, 20000)) or b"{}")
239:                 text = str(body.get("text") or "").strip()
240:                 if len(text) > 500:                      # refused, not silently cut
241:                     raise ValueError("input is longer than 500 characters")
242:                 if not text:
243:                     raise ValueError("empty input")
244:                 if self.path not in ("/api/resolve", "/api/ask", "/api/check",
245:                                      "/api/structured", "/api/explore"):
246:                     return self._send(404, b"{}", "application/json")
247:                 with engine.lock:
248:                     if self.path == "/api/explore":

250:                     elif self.path == "/api/resolve":
251:                         res = engine.resolve(text)
252:                     elif self.path == "/api/ask":

254:                     elif self.path == "/api/structured":
255:                         answer = str(body.get("answer") or "").strip()[:20000]
256:                         if not answer:
257:                             raise ValueError("empty answer")
258:                         res = engine.structured(text, answer)
259:                     else:
260:                         answer = str(body.get("answer") or "").strip()[:4000]
261:                         if not answer:
262:                             raise ValueError("empty answer")
263:                         res = engine.check(text, answer)
264:                 self._send(200, json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False,
265:                                            allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8"),
266:                            "application/json; charset=utf-8")
267:             except Exception as e:  # show the reason on the page, not a dead request
268:                 self._send(400, json.dumps({"error": str(e)}, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
269:                            "application/json; charset=utf-8")

FILE audit_evidence_claims/m21/attacks/SUMMARY.md
﻿# Round 21 attack results

HEAD `e648017a2e3bee68ed4cbf8437f2438374937641`.

## P1: explicit Ce-134-labelled trastuzumab is drawn as unlabelled trastuzumab

Strongest plain-English input: **`trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134`**. Also **`[134Ce] trastuzumab`** and **`134Ce trastuzumab`**. Each selects **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585 / 13 map trials** without any public refusal; trial and sponsor QA each return **12 originator evidence rows**. The entire map and both full evidence arrays equal bare trastuzumab. `assertions.json` verifies this equality, beyond matching a label/count.

The corresponding written-name **`trastuzumab labelled with cerium-134`** refuses with no centre and no QA evidence. So do `cerium-134 trastuzumab`, `134cerium trastuzumab`, `cerium134 trastuzumab`, and `134Ce radiolabelled trastuzumab`.

| Stage | Ce-134 spelling | cerium-134 spelling |
|---|---|---|
| Intervention resolver | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED |
| `_resolver_blocked` | `{}` | `{}` |
| `_qualified` | false | false |
| `_item_has_isotope` | false | true |
| Actual `_marked` return | `None` | refusal |
| `_whole_name` | `None` | `None` |
| Public linker | positive Drug, no Refused | Refused only |
| Map / trial QA / sponsor QA | 13 trials / 12 rows / 12 rows | no centre / 0 / 0 |

`[134Ce] trastuzumab` is especially notable: the intervention resolver reports EXACT after `extract_parenthetical`. This is a complete refusal miss rather than `explore` disregarding a Refused record.

**Product identity evidence:** Bailey et al., *Evaluation of 134Ce as a PET imaging surrogate for antibody drug conjugates incorporating 225Ac*, Nuclear Medicine and Biology 110-111 (2022), 28-36, DOI `10.1016/j.nucmedbio.2022.04.007`; epub **2022-04-22**, print Jul-Aug 2022. The primary paper's abstract explicitly describes [134Ce]Ce-DOTA-Trastuzumab administered to tumour-bearing mice. Accessible indexed primary abstract: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35512517/ . Author-deposited manuscript metadata: https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1866971 . This establishes the labelled construct; interpreting the short plain-English input as that tracer family is an explicit reviewer inference. No therapeutic claim is used in the audit.

**Cause:** `src/query.py:124-136` intentionally includes Ce only in `_NAME_MASS`, not `_MEDICAL_MASS`. `src/textrules.py:290-299` also excludes `ce`, so exact bracketed isotope syntax does not help. The written-name branch (`src/query.py:208-220`) recognizes `cerium` but cannot recognize `Ce`. The item-wide check in `_marked` (`src/query.py:457-459`) therefore returns no refusal. `Engine.explore` selects the remaining Drug (`src/app.py:88-95`). Avoiding prefix false positives such as `75 several` does not require accepting a complete `[134Ce]` label or an explicit `labelled with Ce-134` construction. Recognition can distinguish bounded isotope tokens from arbitrary letter prefixes; implementation was not changed in this review.

Additional same-cause successful reproductions: `Ce-134 trastuzumab`, `134Ce-labelled trastuzumab`, `trastuzumab labelled with 134Ce`, `134Ce DOTA trastuzumab`, `134Ce-DOTA trastuzumab`. All equal the parent map and QA arrays. Fully fused `[134Ce]Ce-DOTA-trastuzumab` and `134Ce-DOTA-trastuzumab` are **not_found**, not leaks. `134Ce trastuzumab, osimertinib` selects trastuzumab without disclosure; reversing the list selects osimertinib but leaves the positive trastuzumab entity.

**Independent same-cause corroboration:** `trastuzumab labelled with Mn-52` and `trastuzumab labelled with 52Mn` also pass every stage and return the same parent map/12+12 evidence rows, whereas `trastuzumab labelled with manganese-52` refuses. A real 52Mn trastuzumab conjugate is documented by Omweri et al., 2024, *Development of 52Mn Labeled Trastuzumab for Extended Time Point PET Imaging of HER2*, DOI `10.1007/s11307-024-01948-4`, PubMed 39192059: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11436409/ . The immediate `52Mn trastuzumab` form does refuse through the earlier isotope-token path, so it is not included among leaks. Er/Se/Cr/Co/La/Fe/Cs symbol forms also leak in software probes, but no independent existence claim is made for those isotope/trastuzumab pairings and they are not needed for this finding.

## Additional remaining label-word coverage gap

`radio-isotope-labelled trastuzumab`, `radioisotope-labelled trastuzumab`, and `trastuzumab labelled with a radioisotope` also pass every guard and produce the complete unlabelled parent map and 12+12 evidence rows. `_LABEL_STEMS` at `src/query.py:179-180` omits `radioisotop`; joining 1-3 words cannot repair absent vocabulary. `radioactive-isotope-labelled trastuzumab` and `radiolabelled trastuzumab` correctly refuse. This is an inherited label-recognition gap, not a HEAD regression, and can be reported as a supplement to the known lexical-coverage class rather than inflating blocker counts.

## Controls and recall limitations

- New therapy-symbol probes Tb, Th, Bi, Sc, Ho, Tl, Xe, Au, Pd, Ir, Ag, Sn, Dy, Pt all refuse in current code, including `[161Tb] trastuzumab`.
- Prior morphology and glued-element cases `trastuzumab radioactively labelled`, `radio-immuno-conjugate trastuzumab`, `radioconjugated trastuzumab`, `trastuzumab labelled with iodine124`, `99mtechnetium trastuzumab`, and `trastuzumab labelled with technetium99m` now refuse.
- `non-radio-labelled trastuzumab` and `non-radiolabelled trastuzumab` now retain the parent correctly, as do `trastuzumab without radiolabel`, `trastuzumab is not radioactive`, and `trastuzumab not radioactively labelled`.
- Bare trastuzumab, Herceptin, cisplatin/radiation, radiotherapy plus cisplatin, osimertinib dose, paclitaxel cycles, lead-compound text and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose controls retain their molecules. `75 several trastuzumab` and `51 criteria trastuzumab` also retain trastuzumab.
- `trastuzumab compared with radioactively labelled controls` newly refuses, while the previous query module accepted it. This is an extension of the explicitly accepted same-list-item over-refusal, not a blocker.
- `trastuzumab without any radiolabel` and `trastuzumab free from radioactive label` still over-refuse (the latter resolver also says BLOCKED_NEGATED). These are inherited negation/recall limitations, not originator leaks.
- The preliminary `57Co bleomycin` exploration found no bleomycin node even for bare bleomycin; it is not a leak and is not used as evidence of a defect.

## Reproducibility and scope

`new_probe.py` reuses the m20 attack harness, replacing only cases, output location and the temporary comparison module name. `reuse_manifest.json` records the adaptation. **87 unique current/previous-query case pairs (174 staged observations)** completed. Full outputs are `new_results.json`; compact outputs `new_summary.json`; exact-equality assertions `assertions.json`; case list `cases.json`. `scan.py`/`scan.json` retain initial exploration and are not additive to the staged-case count.

The previous comparison substitutes **only `HEAD^:src/query.py`** against current other modules and data. Therefore it is a counterfactual module comparison, not an entire historical deployment. Ce/Mn symbol misses and radioisotope-word misses occur in both modules; not all Tb previous results reproduce the old deployment because `textrules.py` is current. Root owns independent HTTP corroboration and comprehensive historical reruns.

All created files are under `audit_evidence_claims/m21/attacks/`. No application/tracked file was changed. Engine connections were replaced by read-only SQLite connections before probes; no model is called by `Engine.ask`.

+## M21-B1 — bounded Ce-134 isotope labels pass every refusal stage (P1)
+
+**Exact input:** `trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134`. `POST /api/explore` returns **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585 / 13 trials**. `Which trials evaluate trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134?` and `Who sponsors trials of trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134?` each return **12 originator evidence rows**. The **entire map and both complete evidence arrays equal bare trastuzumab**. This is an inherited hole, not an originator regression introduced by this commit. [Independent HTTP](checks/independent_m21_http.json), [exact-equality assertions](checks/independent_m21_summary.json), [all-stage trace](attacks/new_results.json).
+
+The paired input `trastuzumab labelled with cerium-134` refuses, has no map centre and returns zero QA evidence. `[134Ce] trastuzumab`, `134Ce trastuzumab`, `Ce-134 trastuzumab`, `134Ce-labelled trastuzumab`, and `134Ce-DOTA trastuzumab` reproduce the miss. `[134Ce] trastuzumab` even receives intervention-resolver **EXACT**, following `extract_parenthetical`. The completely fused `[134Ce]Ce-DOTA-trastuzumab` and `134Ce-DOTA-trastuzumab` are **not_found**, and are not counted as leaks. [Supplemental HTTP](checks/supplement_m21_http.json), [supplemental assertions](checks/supplement_m21_assertions.json).
+
+| Actual stage | `trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134` | `trastuzumab labelled with cerium-134` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Intervention resolver | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED |
+| `_resolver_blocked` | `{}` | `{}` |
+| `_qualified` | false | false |
+| `_item_has_isotope` | false | true |
+| `_marked` | `None` | refusal |
+| `_whole_name` | `None` | `None` |
+| Public linker | Drug, no Refused | Refused only |
+| Map / trial QA / sponsor QA | 13 trials / 12 rows / 12 rows | no centre / 0 / 0 |
+
+**Identity premise and evidence:** a Ce-134-labelled trastuzumab conjugate is a real, distinct research material. Bailey et al., *Evaluation of 134Ce as a PET imaging surrogate for antibody drug conjugates incorporating 225Ac* (2022; online 2022-04-22; DOI 10.1016/j.nucmedbio.2022.04.007), studied `[134Ce]Ce-DOTA-Trastuzumab` in tumour-bearing mice. The short plain-English query's relationship to this tracer family is the reviewer's inference. The paper establishes product distinction; it does not supply graph edges or clinical claims. [Primary paper abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35512517/).
+
+**Cause:** `src/query.py:124-136` puts Ce in `_NAME_MASS` but excludes it from `_MEDICAL_MASS`; `src/textrules.py:290-299` also excludes `ce`. The written-name branch at `src/query.py:208-220` recognizes `cerium`, while the explicit `Ce-134` and `[134Ce]` tokens remain invisible. The item guard at `src/query.py:457-459` returns no refusal, the linker adds a Drug at `src/query.py:613-630`, and `Engine.explore` selects it at `src/app.py:88-95`.
+
+Avoiding false positives for `75 several` and `51 criteria` does not justify accepting a whole bracketed isotope or explicit `labelled with Ce-134`. A repair must distinguish bounded isotope tokens from prefixes of ordinary words. Required outcome: refusal or the correct distinct product, with no unlabelled-parent map/QA substitution. No implementation was changed in this review.
+
+**Same-cause corroboration:** `trastuzumab labelled with Mn-52` likewise returns the parent map and both evidence arrays, whereas `trastuzumab labelled with manganese-52` refuses. A 52Mn-labelled trastuzumab construct is documented in Omweri et al. (2024), DOI 10.1007/s11307-024-01948-4. [Primary study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11436409/). The immediate `52Mn trastuzumab` form refuses and is not claimed as a leak. Er/Se/Cr/Co/La/Fe/Cs observations are retained as software probes; their isotope/trastuzumab pairings are not needed to prove this blocker.
+
+## M21-B2 — an explicit radioisotope-labelled product is treated as unlabelled (P1)
+
+**Exact inputs:** `radioisotope-labelled trastuzumab` and `trastuzumab labelled with a radioisotope`. The split spelling `radio-isotope-labelled trastuzumab` corroborates the defect. All return the **complete bare-TRASTUZUMAB map and the same 12 trial / 12 sponsor evidence rows**. `radiolabelled trastuzumab` and `radioactive-isotope-labelled trastuzumab` correctly refuse. [HTTP](checks/supplement_m21_http.json), [equality/control assertions](checks/supplement_m21_assertions.json), [stage assertions](attacks/assertions.json).
+
+Every guard misses: resolver has no BLOCKED result, `_resolver_blocked` is `{}`, `_qualified` and `_item_has_isotope` are false, `_marked` and `_whole_name` return `None`, and the public linker supplies a positive Drug without Refused. The actual page form renders the parent SVG centre and CHEMBL1201585 trail. [Rendered main captures](contract/ui_m21_http.json), [rendered supplementary captures](contract/ui_supplement_m21_http.json).
+
+**Cause:** `_LABEL_STEMS` at `src/query.py:179-180` omits `radioisotop`; `_LABEL_WORDS` at `src/query.py:184-186` also lacks it. The 1–3-word concatenation loop at `src/query.py:200-206` cannot recover missing vocabulary. The same positive-link selection path follows. Both current and previous query-module probes miss it; it is an inherited gap newly reproduced this round.
+
+This is independent of B1: these inputs supply no element/mass for an isotope table to recognize, while adding this label stem would not fix `[134Ce] trastuzumab`. Both violate the requested all-stage refusal approval bar. The conditional docstring wording is not being interpreted as `explore` ignoring a Refused object: the error is that no stage produces one for an explicitly modified product.
+
+## Latest repairs and ordinary controls
+
+- **M20-B1 FIXED for every original tested spelling:** Tb/terbium, Th/thorium and Bi/bismuth no longer draw the parent; new-table Sc/Ho/Tl/Xe/Au/Pd/Ir/Ag/Sn/Dy/Pt probes also refuse.

+- Bare trastuzumab/Herceptin, `radiotherapy plus cisplatin`, `cisplatin and radiation`, `osimertinib 80 mg`, `paclitaxel 2 cycles`, `75 several trastuzumab`, `51 criteria trastuzumab`, and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose retain expected identities.
+- `trastuzumab compared with radioactively labelled controls` newly refuses in the query-module comparison. This extends the user's accepted same-list-item over-refusal and is **not a blocker**.
+- The user-accepted M5-S2, rapamycin forms, Trastuzumab--vcmmae conjugate, 9-amino-20(s)-camptothecin, il-6ra, TAK-659F, GS-11CAL-101, 3en3hg4wsw and same-item over-refusals remain separately identified in the historical matrices. The bevacizumab development-code synonym limitation is not counted as a code blocker.

+"""Assemble the independent review from this round's fresh evidence only."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+import posixpath
+import re
+
+OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+
+
+def read(path):
+    return (OUT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
+
+
+def data(path):
+    return json.loads(read(path))
+
+
+def relocate_links(text, directory):
+    def replacement(match):
+        target = match.group(1)
+        if target.startswith(("http://", "https://", "#", "/")):
+            return match.group(0)
+        return "](" + posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(directory, target)) + ")"
+    return re.sub(r"\]\(([^)]+)\)", replacement, text)
+

+## M21-B1 — bounded Ce-134 isotope labels pass every refusal stage (P1)
+
+**Exact input:** `trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134`. `POST /api/explore` returns **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585 / 13 trials**. `Which trials evaluate trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134?` and `Who sponsors trials of trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134?` each return **12 originator evidence rows**. The **entire map and both complete evidence arrays equal bare trastuzumab**. This is an inherited hole, not an originator regression introduced by this commit. [Independent HTTP](checks/independent_m21_http.json), [exact-equality assertions](checks/independent_m21_summary.json), [all-stage trace](attacks/new_results.json).
+
+The paired input `trastuzumab labelled with cerium-134` refuses, has no map centre and returns zero QA evidence. `[134Ce] trastuzumab`, `134Ce trastuzumab`, `Ce-134 trastuzumab`, `134Ce-labelled trastuzumab`, and `134Ce-DOTA trastuzumab` reproduce the miss. `[134Ce] trastuzumab` even receives intervention-resolver **EXACT**, following `extract_parenthetical`. The completely fused `[134Ce]Ce-DOTA-trastuzumab` and `134Ce-DOTA-trastuzumab` are **not_found**, and are not counted as leaks. [Supplemental HTTP](checks/supplement_m21_http.json), [supplemental assertions](checks/supplement_m21_assertions.json).
+
+| Actual stage | `trastuzumab labelled with Ce-134` | `trastuzumab labelled with cerium-134` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Intervention resolver | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED | CONTAINED_ALIAS + UNRESOLVED; no BLOCKED |
+| `_resolver_blocked` | `{}` | `{}` |
+| `_qualified` | false | false |
+| `_item_has_isotope` | false | true |
+| `_marked` | `None` | refusal |
+| `_whole_name` | `None` | `None` |
+| Public linker | Drug, no Refused | Refused only |
+| Map / trial QA / sponsor QA | 13 trials / 12 rows / 12 rows | no centre / 0 / 0 |
+
+**Identity premise and evidence:** a Ce-134-labelled trastuzumab conjugate is a real, distinct research material. Bailey et al., *Evaluation of 134Ce as a PET imaging surrogate for antibody drug conjugates incorporating 225Ac* (2022; online 2022-04-22; DOI 10.1016/j.nucmedbio.2022.04.007), studied `[134Ce]Ce-DOTA-Trastuzumab` in tumour-bearing mice. The short plain-English query's relationship to this tracer family is the reviewer's inference. The paper establishes product distinction; it does not supply graph edges or clinical claims. [Primary paper abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35512517/).
+
+**Cause:** `src/query.py:124-136` puts Ce in `_NAME_MASS` but excludes it from `_MEDICAL_MASS`; `src/textrules.py:290-299` also excludes `ce`. The written-name branch at `src/query.py:208-220` recognizes `cerium`, while the explicit `Ce-134` and `[134Ce]` tokens remain invisible. The item guard at `src/query.py:457-459` returns no refusal, the linker adds a Drug at `src/query.py:613-630`, and `Engine.explore` selects it at `src/app.py:88-95`.
+
+Avoiding false positives for `75 several` and `51 criteria` does not justify accepting a whole bracketed isotope or explicit `labelled with Ce-134`. A repair must distinguish bounded isotope tokens from prefixes of ordinary words. Required outcome: refusal or the correct distinct product, with no unlabelled-parent map/QA substitution. No implementation was changed in this review.
+
+**Same-cause corroboration:** `trastuzumab labelled with Mn-52` likewise returns the parent map and both evidence arrays, whereas `trastuzumab labelled with manganese-52` refuses. A 52Mn-labelled trastuzumab construct is documented in Omweri et al. (2024), DOI 10.1007/s11307-024-01948-4. [Primary study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11436409/). The immediate `52Mn trastuzumab` form refuses and is not claimed as a leak. Er/Se/Cr/Co/La/Fe/Cs observations are retained as software probes; their isotope/trastuzumab pairings are not needed to prove this blocker.
+

+**Cause:** `_LABEL_STEMS` at `src/query.py:179-180` omits `radioisotop`; `_LABEL_WORDS` at `src/query.py:184-186` also lacks it. The 1–3-word concatenation loop at `src/query.py:200-206` cannot recover missing vocabulary. The same positive-link selection path follows. Both current and previous query-module probes miss it; it is an inherited gap newly reproduced this round.
+
+This is independent of B1: these inputs supply no element/mass for an isotope table to recognize, while adding this label stem would not fix `[134Ce] trastuzumab`. Both violate the requested all-stage refusal approval bar. The conditional docstring wording is not being interpreted as `explore` ignoring a Refused object: the error is that no stage produces one for an explicitly modified product.
